title: Choose the visual world for PHOENIX
question: The roll assigned Civic Service. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. All options honour your brief: clean, minimal, Phosphor icons, no icon tiles.

options.label: Civic Service
options.lineage: Public-service design systems (GOV.UK, USWDS) and their plain, trusted forms
options.thesis: PHOENIX reads like a public service you already trust: plain ink, strong type, nothing decorative.
options.viewport: Ink header band with the mark and nav; a left column holding the SOS action as a large red block, right column a time-ranked ledger of your alerts and incidents with status as a numbered step rail.
options.risk: Can read bureaucratic if the type scale is timid or spacing goes loose.

raised.raise: Lists are fixed-column ledgers: rows are live entities ranked by time and columns never move.
One body size does the work; hierarchy comes from weight and space, not a ladder of sizes.
The SOS screen gives one thing the whole viewport: the action, nothing beside it.
Nothing is labelled twice: no icon echoing its own label, no caption restating a heading.

options.label: Safety Signage
options.lineage: ISO 7010 safety signs and emergency wayfinding
options.thesis: State is spoken in the safety-sign code everyone already reads: green safe, yellow caution, red danger, blue required.
options.viewport: White ground, a green 'you are safe' status plate across the top that turns red when an SOS is live; below, square-cut panels for incidents and contacts.
options.risk: The most familiar answer for a safety product, and four strong hues fight a minimal brief.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: Boarding pass and live airport gate board
options.thesis: Every alert is a pass with a number; the command center is a live board that reranks in place.
options.viewport: Your active SOS as a segmented pass (ID, time, coordinates, status); below it a board of incidents ranked by time, changed rows lit amber until seen.
options.case: Strong for admin clarity; citizens identify less with travel than with public service.
options.risk: Can tip into airport costume if the pass is drawn too literally.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Alerts as rows on a flap board.
options.case: Loses both axes: dark board is a costume on a calm citizen app.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.case: Loses both axes: too ornamental for minimal.
options.kept: One body size does the work.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.case: Loses both axes: wrong model for lists and admin.
options.kept: SOS screen gives one thing the whole viewport.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything coded by number and colour.
options.case: Loses both axes: coded labels hurt clarity in an emergency.

options.label: Guide Map
options.thesis: Areas as swelling lobes of colour.
options.case: Loses both axes: playful tone wrong for emergencies.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS dashboard: sidebar, stat row, tables, one blue accent, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar left, page title, a row of plain numbers, then tables of alerts and incidents.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every admin template by design.
